title: First-Day Viewers Slam Yash's 'Toxic' for Messy Screenplay Despite Record Advance Sales
excerpt: Yash's long-awaited return to theatres draws sharp criticism for writing and pacing, though his screen presence and the film's visuals earn scattered praise.
body:
• Yash's Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups opened in theatres on August 26 to largely negative early audience reactions on X, with viewers criticising the screenplay, editing, and pacing.
  • The film recorded Rs 43.64 crore in India Day 1 advance booking gross and over Rs 70 crore across all markets, making it one of 2026's biggest openers.
  • Yash plays a dual role as gangster Raya and his estranged son Rumi in the post-independence Goa-set period action thriller directed by Geetu Mohandas.
  • Kiara Advani's performance as Nadia has drawn praise even from viewers who found the overall film disappointing.

Kannada superstar Yash returned to theatres on August 26 with Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, his first major release since KGF: Chapter 2 four years ago. The gangster drama, directed by Geetu Mohandas, arrived with record pre-release numbers — but early audience reactions have been sharply critical of the film's storytelling.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=utdcE0x6-ag

Audience Reactions Split on Style vs Substance

Within hours of the first shows, X was flooded with reactions that largely panned the film's screenplay and editing. One reviewer called it "a disaster of the decade," rating the film 2 out of 5. Another described the first half as carrying a "Heavy KGF hangover" with "a very clumsy and tiring screenplay" and artificial-looking action sequences.

"First half of #TOXIC was straight up torture. Feels like watching a 90-minute trailer — editing is completely off, zero emotional connection, and scene after scene just drags on."

— X user @RnsRns88518967

The three-hour runtime drew particular frustration. One prominent post labelled the film "a technically sound film buried under chaotic writing and exhausting execution," noting that proper character introductions are largely absent and the narrative lacks clear flow. Several viewers also criticised the intimate scenes, calling them forced, while the background score by Ravi Basrur — a standout element in the KGF franchise — was described as a "major letdown."

Yash's Star Power and Kiara Advani Earn Praise

Even the harshest reviews acknowledged Yash's magnetic screen presence. The Kannada star plays a dual role as Raya, an ageing gangster, and his estranged son Rumi — also known as Ticket — who returns seeking revenge after being abandoned. Viewers praised the high-voltage action set pieces and striking production design.

Kiara Advani, playing Nadia, emerged as a bright spot. "Toxic is a different world in itself. Leading ladies have solid roles, movie runs high on emotions and feelings. Kiara is fantastic," one viewer wrote. Nayanthara as Raya's sister Ganga and the emotional interplay between her and Yash also drew appreciation.

A minority of viewers rated the film highly. One gave it 4 out of 5, calling Yash "a TRUE Pan-India Superstar" and praising the "strong character establishment" and "absolutely stunning" visuals in the first half.

Record Advance Booking Despite Polarised Reception

The film entered release day with massive pre-sale numbers. According to Sacnilk, India Day 1 advance booking gross stood at Rs 43.64 crore, including block seats, as of 1 pm on August 25. Reported advance sales across all markets had crossed Rs 70 crore, with the Telugu market alone contributing around Rs 15 crore in gross pre-sales. In the UK, the film reportedly secured more than 400 screens.

Production delays had pushed the release from its original April 2025 date by 503 days. Yash co-produced the film alongside Venkat K. Narayana under KVN Productions and Monster Mind Creations. The ensemble cast also includes Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria, Rukmini Vasanth, and Akshay Oberoi.

What Comes Next

The film's opening-day box office performance will determine whether the pre-release momentum can withstand the critical backlash. Set against the backdrop of a crowded Onam week release slate, Toxic faces the challenge of converting massive advance bookings into sustained theatre runs amid a first-day reception that has been, at best, deeply divided.
